raw_case_text:
An 8-month old baby boy presented with high-grade fever associated with chills and rigours for 15 days, abdominal distension for 5 days and diarrhoea for 5 days. He also had an erythematous rash over his face and back. On examination, his length was 73 cm (85th percentile) and weight was 7.3 kg (3rd percentile). He was afebrile, heart rate was 140/min, respiratory rate was 38/min and blood pressure was 102/74 mm Hg. Abdominal examination revealed mild hepatomegaly. No neck stiffness or signs of meningeal irritation were seen. Investigations revealed a haemoglobin of 7.2 gm/dL; total white cell count, 8300/mm3 (neutrophils, 30%; lymphocytes, 69%; eosinophils, 0%; monocytes, 1%; basophils, 0%); and platelets, 81,000/mm3. Peripheral smear for malarial parasites was negative. Tests for dengue fever were negative. Widal test revealed the antibody titers to 'O' and 'H' antigens to be 1:160 each respectively. Liver function tests showed an elevation of the hepatic enzymes - alanine aminotransferase (ALT), 94 IU/L; aspartate aminotransferase (AST), 249 IU/L; and INR, 1.3. international normalized ratio (INR) Serum creatinine was 0.4 mg/dL. Urine examination and echocardiography were both normal. Ultrasound examination of the abdomen revealed mild hepatosplenomegaly with increased echogenicity of liver. Blood culture showed S. typhi sensitive to ampicillin-sulbactam and cotrimoxazole but resistant to fluoroquinolones and third-generation cephalosporins. The blood culture results were obtained on day 6 of admission. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination showed lymphocytic pleocytosis (14 leucocytes/mm3 with 100% lymphocytes), 38 mg/dL of proteins and 74 mg/dL of glucose. CSF Gram stain, Zeil Neilson stain and culture were negative.
The child was initially treated with IV ceftriaxone (100 mg/kg/day) for 5 days but had no response. Antibiotics were changed to IV aztreonam and oral azithromycin (20 mg/kg/day) which were given for 5 days but still the fever persisted. Hence, antibiotics were switched to IV meropenem (40 mg/kg/dose 8 hourly), and oral azithromycin was continued. The fever subsided in 13 days. IV meropenem was given for 14 days and oral azithromycin was given for 7 days.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 8-month-old male infant presented with high-grade fever with chills and rigors for 15 days, abdominal distension for 5 days, and diarrhea for 5 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: High-grade fever accompanied by chills and rigors began 15 days prior to admission. Ten days later, he developed progressive abdominal distension, diarrhea, and an erythematous rash over his face and back.
subjective.review_of_systems: Erythematous rash over face and back, chills, rigors.

objective.physical_examination: Length: 73 cm (85th percentile), weight: 7.3 kg (3rd percentile). Afebrile at examination; heart rate 140/min, respiratory rate 38/min, blood pressure 102/74 mmHg. Abdomen: mild hepatomegaly. Neurological: no neck stiffness or signs of meningeal irritation. Skin: erythematous rash over face and back.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin: 7.2 g/dL; total white cell count: 8,300/mm3 (neutrophils 30%, lymphocytes 69%, eosinophils 0%, monocytes 1%, basophils 0%); platelets: 81,000/mm3. Peripheral smear for malarial parasites: negative. Dengue tests: negative. Liver function tests: ALT 94 IU/L, AST 249 IU/L, INR 1.3. Serum creatinine: 0.4 mg/dL. Urinalysis: normal. Echocardiography: normal. Abdominal ultrasound: mild hepatosplenomegaly with increased echogenicity of the liver.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar puncture (CSF): lymphocytic pleocytosis (14 leukocytes/mm3 with 100% lymphocytes), protein 38 mg/dL, glucose 74 mg/dL. CSF Gram stain, Ziehl-Neelsen stain, and CSF bacterial culture were negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Typhoid fever due to multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi with reactive CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis (meningism). Blood culture isolated Salmonella Typhi sensitive to ampicillin-sulbactam and co-trimoxazole, but resistant to fluoroquinolones and third-generation cephalosporins; Widal test showed antibody titers to 'O' and 'H' antigens of 1:160 each. Antimicrobial management: initial IV ceftriaxone (100 mg/kg/day) for 5 days showed no response; switched to IV aztreonam and oral azithromycin (20 mg/kg/day) for 5 days with persistent fever; successfully treated with escalation to IV meropenem (40 mg/kg/dose every 8 h) for 14 days and oral azithromycin for 7 days. Fever resolved completely on day 13 with full recovery.
